questions.q: Name the major nutrients in our food.
questions.a: Carbohydrates, fats, proteins, vitamins, minerals, plus dietary fibre and water.

questions.q: Which nutrients give us energy mainly?
questions.a: Carbohydrates and fats are the chief energy-giving foods.

questions.q: Why are proteins called body-building nutrients?
questions.a: They help the body grow and repair damaged tissues.

questions.q: How do we test a food item for starch?
questions.a: Put iodine solution on it - a blue-black colour shows starch is present.

questions.q: What colour shows a positive starch test?
questions.a: Blue-black, when iodine solution meets starch.

questions.q: Which foods would give a positive starch test?
questions.a: Rice, potato, bread and wheat flour.

questions.q: How is the test for protein done?
questions.a: Add copper sulphate and caustic soda solutions to the food paste - violet colour means protein.

questions.q: What colour indicates protein in a food test?
questions.a: Violet colour after adding copper sulphate and caustic soda.

questions.q: Name two protein-rich foods.
questions.a: Pulses, milk, eggs, fish and paneer.

questions.q: How do we test food for fats?
questions.a: Press the food on paper - an oily patch that does not dry shows fat.

questions.q: What is observed when a potato piece is pressed on paper?
questions.a: No oily patch - potato stores starch, not fat.

questions.q: Name two fat-rich foods.
questions.a: Butter, ghee, nuts and oilseeds.

concepts.title: Carbohydrates and Fats as Energy Sources

questions.q: Why does our body need energy-giving food?
questions.a: Carbohydrates and fats release energy for working, playing and even sleeping (breathing, heartbeat).

questions.q: Name two carbohydrate-rich and two fat-rich foods.
questions.a: Carbohydrates: rice, potato. Fats: ghee, groundnut.

questions.q: What happens if we eat more energy food than we burn?
questions.a: Extra energy is stored as fat and body weight increases.

questions.q: What do proteins do for the body?
questions.a: They build new tissues, repair worn-out parts and help growth.

questions.q: Name two protein-rich foods for children.
questions.a: Milk, dal, eggs, fish and soyabean.

questions.q: What happens to children who get too little protein?
questions.a: Growth slows; severe lack causes kwashiorkor (swollen belly, weak muscles).

questions.q: Why do we need vitamins and minerals only in small amounts?
questions.a: They are protective foods - tiny quantities keep the body working well and fight disease.

questions.q: Name the vitamin that protects eyes and its source.
questions.a: Vitamin A - from carrots, papaya, green leafy vegetables; lack causes night blindness.

questions.q: Which mineral keeps bones strong and where is it found?
questions.a: Calcium - in milk and milk products.

questions.q: What is dietary fibre (roughage) and why do we need it?
questions.a: Indigestible plant fibre that helps remove undigested food and prevents constipation.

questions.q: Name two foods rich in roughage.
questions.a: Whole grains, fresh fruits, vegetables and salads.

questions.q: Why is water essential even though it gives no energy?
questions.a: It carries nutrients in the body, removes wastes and controls body temperature.

concepts.title: Balanced Diet and Preservation of Nutrients

questions.q: What is a balanced diet?
questions.a: A meal containing all nutrients - carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, fibre and water - in right amounts.

questions.q: Why should food not be washed after cutting vegetables?
questions.a: Washing washes away water-soluble vitamins; also overcooking destroys vitamins.

questions.q: How does junk food harm a balanced diet?
questions.a: It fills the stomach with fats and little else, crowding out protective nutrients.

questions.q: What are deficiency diseases?
questions.a: Diseases caused by long lack of a nutrient - scurvy (vitamin C), rickets (vitamin D), goitre (iodine).

questions.q: Name the disease from lack of vitamin C and its symptom.
questions.a: Scurvy - bleeding gums and slow healing wounds; citrus fruits cure it.

questions.q: Why do poor children often suffer from deficiency diseases?
questions.a: Their diet lacks variety - protective nutrients are missing from meagre meals.
